To represent the aquatic observation data extracted from factsheet application. An aquatic observation refers to a specific year, is about an aquatic resource, and is situated in a given habitat, in which the aquatic species from the resource live. Observations can have a reporting year that is different from the observation time.
column9: For an aquatic resource, what species, in what fishing areas, climatic zones, bottom types, depth zones, geo forms, horizontal and vertical distribution, and for what standardized abundance level, exploitation state and rate, have been observed? for what reference year? At what year the observation has been recorded?

column8: To represent aquatic resources or stocks as composed of aquatic organisms from one or more species, and living in a water area.
column9: What species are present in this aquatic resource/stock? In what water area this aquatic resource/stock lives in?

column8: To model bags of items (elements). The Bag is characterized by a collection that can have multiple copies of each object.
column9: What bag is this item an element of?; What is the size of this bag?; What resource does this item refer to?; What are the items contained in this bag?

column8: The basic plans. This content ontology design patterns represents plans descriptions and their executions. It is defined by combining and expanding other CPs: basic plans description, basic plans execution, and object role. Expansion involves the partial clone of ontology elements from DOLCE Ultra Lite and Plans Lite ontologies.

The basic plans execution content ontology design pattern represents the execution of a plan and the entity that participate in such an execution. This CP is the composition of other CPs: situation and region. Furthermore, it expands such CPs with ontology elements that are partial clones of elements from the DOCLE Ultra Lite and the Plans Lite ontologies.
The pattern intends to model the domain of born digital archives.
column9: What are the main entities (units) that compose born digital archives? These are fonds, series, files and items. What is the hierarchy of units within a born digital archive? Fonds composed from series or files, series composed from files and files composed from items. Who is the creator of an archive? The creator is entity of type foaf:Agent.

column8: The DOLCE+DnS Ultralite ontology. It is a simplification of some parts of the DOLCE Lite-Plus library (cf. http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DLP397.owl). Main aspects in which DOLCE+DnS Ultralite departs from DOLCE Lite-Plus are the following: - The names of classes and relations have been made more intuitive - The DnS-related part is closer to the newer 'constructive DnS' ontology (http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/cDnS.owl). - Temporal and spatial relations are simplified - Qualities and regions are more relaxed than in DOLCE-Full: they can be used as attributes of any entity; an axiom states that each quality has a region - Axiomatization makes use of simpler constructs than DOLCE Lite-Plus - The architecture of the ontology is pattern-based, which means that DOLCE+DnS Ultralite is also available in modules, called 'content ontology design patterns', which can be applied independently in the design of domain ontologies (cf. http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org). If many modules are needed in a same ontology project, it is anyway useful to use this integrated version. The final result is a lightweight, easy-to-apply foundational ontology for modeling either physical or social contexts. Several extensions of DOLCE+DnS Ultralite have been designed: - Information objects: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/IOLite.owl - Systems: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/SystemsLite.owl - Plans: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/PlansLite.owl - Legal domain: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/CLO/CoreLegal.owl - Lexical and semiotic domains: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/lmm/LMM_L2.owl - DOLCE-Zero: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/d0.owl is a commonsense-oriented generalisation of some top-level classes, which allows to use DOLCE with tolerance against ambiguities like abstract vs. concrete information, locations vs. physical artifacts, event occurrences vs. event types, events vs. situations, qualities vs. regions, etc.; etc.

The ICEs cover title, abbreviation, subject area, file format, specification, version, license, citation, standard, repository, external identifiers and textual entities such as keywords, requirements and affiliations.

Models the implementation relationship between a resource and the agent that produced it: a MatWerk project is a process whose participant (task area, infrastructure use case or participant project) realizes a role, and whose output is an NFDI resource such as a dataset, tool, software or digital service. The shortcut property mwo:implementedBy links the resource directly to the process that produced it.
column9: Which tools were developed, co-developed, or adopted in an organization?

column8: Models a service process in which an organization participates and realizes a service provider role; the process generates a service product that realizes a service product role and is linked to a service specification. It applies Pattern 1 to services, giving a structured link between process, participant, roles, output and specification.

Represents temporal regions in BFO terms, distinguishing a zero-dimensional temporal region (an instant such as the start or end of an event) from a one-dimensional temporal region (an interval with a duration), related by occupies_temporal_region, has_first_instance and has_last_instance. Data about those regions - start date, end date, duration, frequency - is carried by specification datum individuals linked to their values with nfdicore:hasValue.

Represents the data values attached to Information Content Entities: any value from the other patterns is linked to its ICE with the nfdicore:hasValue data property. For measurement data the measured value is given with hasValue while the corresponding unit is linked to an instance of iao:MeasurementUnitLabel.
The nary participation pattern. This pattern re-uses participation and situation patterns. It is extracted from DOLCE-UltraLite by partial clone of elements.

The pattern can be used for modelling situations in which we are not certain that a particular actual event has the properties which were described in a news message. We want to define the properties of an actual event which were reported (time, place, actors, subevents, cause, effect etc.), but not to treat them as universal, verified knowledge. The pattern also allows to define who is responsible for a particular description of an event and how this description is dealt with.
column9: In addition to the competency questions defined for pattern ReportingEvent (http:/ontologydesignpatterns.org/wiki/Submissions:ReportingEvent) the pattern allows to answer the following questions: - What aspects of an actual event were presented in the news message? - Who reported an actual event? Which news provider they represented? - When was a certain actual event reported for the first time? - What actual events are presented in a certain medium/by media of a certain news provider? - How was an actual event presented?

column8: An entity individual typed nfdi:NFDI_0000102 (agent) carries identity and label, while each descriptive value is a separate value-node individual reached by obo:IAO_0000235 (denoted by) rather than a direct literal. Agent subsumes people, organizations and consortia.
column9: Which agents (people, organisations, consortia) does the knowledge graph know?; Which agent is responsible for a given resource?

column8: A data portal (nfdi:NFDI_0000123) is distinguished from the repository that hosts it (nfdi:NFDI_0001202), and the formats and standards it supports are separate individuals rather than strings. Its access point is carried by the nfdi:NFDI_0001008 (has url) datatype property.
column9: Which data portals and repositories does NFDI-MatWerk reference?; Which organisation hosts a given portal, and what access conditions apply?; Which data formats and PID systems does a given repository support?

column8: A dataset (nfdi:NFDI_0000009) is described by value nodes reached with obo:IAO_0000235, composed with obo:BFO_0000051 (has part), and related to its subject matter with obo:IAO_0000136 (is about). Creators and affiliations are modelled as ordered list individuals rather than repeated literals.
column9: Which datasets does NFDI-MatWerk provide, and under which licence?; Who created a given dataset, and at which organisation?; Which dataset is described by a given metadata standard?; Which datasets relate to a given material or academic discipline?

column8: An academic event (nfdi:NFDI_0010020, conference) is an occurrent located in time with obo:BFO_0000199, with organisers and audience attached as participants via obo:RO_0000057 and headcount as an input via obo:RO_0002233. Recurrence and title are separate value nodes.
column9: Which academic events has NFDI-MatWerk organised, and when?; Which organisation or task area organised a given event, and how often does it recur?; Which publications or educational materials came out of a given event?

column8: An organization (obo:OBI_0000245) is placed with obo:RO_0001025 (located in) against a city and country, and identified by a ROR identifier value node plus an acronym annotation. Identification and location are modelled as separate reusable individuals, not as literals on the organization.
column9: Which organisations participate in NFDI-MatWerk?; What is an organisation's ROR identifier, and in which city is it located?; Which organisation is the parent of a given institute?; Which researchers, instruments and facilities belong to a given organisation?

column8: A persistent identifier (nfdi:NFDI_0001037, digital object identifier) is a first-class individual that is part-of the object it identifies via obo:BFO_0000050 and carries its resolvable address through nfdi:NFDI_0001008 (has url). The identifier is therefore describable in its own right rather than being a literal on the dataset.
column9: Which FAIR Digital Objects has NFDI-MatWerk registered?; What is the persistent identifier of a given FDO, and which dataset does it denote?

column8: A person (nfdi:NFDI_0000004) carries identity and label while given name, family name and ORCID identifier are separate value-node individuals reached by obo:IAO_0000235. Involvement in a task area or project is modelled with obo:RO_0000056 (participates in) rather than a direct affiliation literal.
column9: Which researchers are involved in NFDI-MatWerk, and in which task area?; What is the ORCID iD of a given researcher, and which organisation are they affiliated with?; Which academic disciplines does a researcher work in?; Which datasets, software or publications is a given researcher a creator of?

column8: A process individual links participants via obo:RO_0000057, realizes one or more roles via obo:BFO_0000055, and is bounded in time by obo:BFO_0000199 (occupies temporal region). This is the join point between the agent, role and temporal patterns.
column9: Which processes are recorded in the knowledge graph, and who participates in them?; Which role is realised in a given process, and over which period?

column8: A publication (nfdi:NFDI_0000190) is tied to the publishing process that produced it (nfdi:NFDI_0000014) through obo:RO_0000056, so the act of publishing is reified rather than collapsed into a date literal. Ordered authorship is an author-list individual and the DOI is a first-class identifier individual.
column9: Which publications resulted from a given task area or infrastructure use case?; What is the DOI of a given publication, and who are its authors in order?; Which publications describe a given software, dataset or instrument?; In which year and through which publishing process did a publication appear?

column8: A role (here nfdi:NFDI_0000114, contact point role) is a first-class individual that is role-of an agent via obo:RO_0000081, rather than an attribute of the agent. Its descriptive values, such as an email address, hang off it as value nodes reached by obo:IAO_0000235.
column9: Which role does a given person or organisation bear, and in what context?; Which contact point is responsible for a given resource?

column8: A service product (nfdi:NFDI_0000232) is the output of a service process via obo:RO_0002353, and the provider is attached by the service product role rather than by a direct provider link. A separate service specification individual holds what the service promises.
column9: Which services does NFDI-MatWerk offer, and who provides them?; Which service supports a given infrastructure use case?; How is a given service accessed, and by whom is it maintained?

column8: Software (nfdi:NFDI_0000121) is described by a composition of distinct value-node classes: title, repository, licence, version number, programming language and operating system, each reached through obo:IAO_0000235. Links to the discipline and the method it implements use obo:RO_0000056 and nfdi:NFDI_0000226.
column9: Which software does NFDI-MatWerk provide, and under which licence?; Where is the source-code repository of a given software, and what is its version?; Which software supports a given workflow or academic discipline?; Who develops and maintains a given software?

column8: A queryable endpoint (nfdi:NFDI_0001095) is modelled as a part of the dataset it serves, linked with obo:BFO_0000051 (has part), rather than as a property of the dataset. This keeps the endpoint addressable and separately describable.
column9: Which SPARQL endpoints can the MatWerk Knowledge Graph be federated with?; What is the endpoint URL of a given knowledge graph, and under which licence is it offered?; Who created and maintains a given endpoint's dataset?

column8: An organisational work unit is modelled as an objective specification (obo:IAO_0000005) that is decomposed into work-package textual entities with obo:BFO_0000051 and is the subject of the processes carrying it out via nfdi:NFDI_0000226. The unit is thus represented by what it specifies rather than as an opaque organisational node.
column9: Which task areas comprise NFDI-MatWerk, and what responsibilities does each hold?; Which researchers and organizations participate in a specified task area?; What infrastructure use cases and participant projects does a task area encompass?

column8: A one-dimensional temporal region (obo:BFO_0000038) is reified as an individual whose extent is given by obo:BFO_0000222 (has first instant) and obo:BFO_0000224 (has last instant) pointing at zero-dimensional regions. Other entities attach to it through obo:BFO_0000199.
column9: Over which period did a given project, event or role run?; Which resources were created or published in a given year?

column8: The Music Note ODP models a symbolic note and its symbolic attributes.
column9: what is the name of a note?, what part of the score does a note belong to?, what are the dynamic indications referring to a note in the score?, what is the fundamental frequency of a note?, what are the different frequencies that make up the spectrum of a note?, what is the duration in seconds of a note, in a given performance?, how is the envelope of a note shaped?

column8: An object can have different states for which different restrictions apply. The goal of the pattern is to allow modelling the different states of an object and the restrictions on such object for its different states
column9: Objects in StateA must have at least one value for property property1; Objects in StateB must have at most one value for property property2; Objects in StateC must have exactly one value for property property3; Objects must have a unique state; Object states must belong to a single collection of non-duplicate elements (i.e., to a set); An object can have three different states; The possible states are: StateA, StateB and StateC

column8: This pattern relies on both the SSN ontology and DUL in order to represent sensors and other techniqually needed objects to deploy a network in a smart home environment. The concept of Network is modeled in this pattern as a System (http://purl.oclc.org/NET/ssnx/ssn#System) whose constituents are NodeStations (subclass of Node which is in turn subsumed by the class http://purl.oclc.org/NET/ssnx/ssn#Device). Another subsumee of the Device class is the class Node describing more details about the content of each node station. Depending on their roles, nodes of a network are devided into types of node senders (whcih observe a phenomenon and send the data) and receivers (which receive the observation data).

column8: This pattern relies on both the SSN ontology and DUL in order to represent an object in the context of Smart Home. Using this model we categorize the objects in to two groups of Smart Objects and NodeHolder based on the reason behind their existance in a smart home. Due to usual difficulties to install sensors in a smart home environment it is common that some other objects (i.e. NodeHolder) are used to attache sensors on so as to observe the situation of other objects (i.e. SmartObject) specifically for the configuration planner. Using this pattern we are able to diffrentiate between these two types of objects. This pattern also allows us to extend the definition of an object's properties in the context of smart home. The properties of a SmartObject which are the interest of the sensing process can be defined as either a subclass of the class http://purl.oclc.org/NET/ssnx/ssn#Property (e.g. the temperature of a stove) or as part of the smart object (e.g. the door of a friedge)
